## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #194 replaces the over-scoped public `/release` route direction from PR #192 with the requested “still useful” shape.

- Release publish validates `.agent/package.json`, tag target state, and GitHub Release creation/update inputs.

## Review
The PR is correctly scoped and follows the linked #192/#193 simplification guidance. Two warning-level issues remain: one publish behavior bug and one misleading prepare failure path.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Existing-release updates drop false publish flags | WARNING | `update_existing=true` with `draft=false` or `prerelease=false` omits the explicit false flags needed by `gh release edit`, so the workflow can report success while leaving release state unchanged. |
| Issue creation URL parse failures become misleading dispatch failures | WARNING | If `createIssue` returns a URL that does not end in digits, prepare emits an empty `issue_number` and the later dispatch step fails with a generic missing env error. |
| Non-blocking diagnostics and coverage gaps remain | INFO | One reviewer noted `releaseUrl()` swallows all `gh release view` errors and that some edge-case tests are thin; these are useful follow-ups but less concrete than the two warnings above. |

## Progress
- The implementation matches the requested scope: no public `/release` route, technical versioning docs only, and manual source-repo-gated Actions.
- Rubrics review passed and found no blocking or warning-level rubric issues.
- Existing inline review comments were empty before posting.
- Posted 2 inline comments: [`publish-release.ts:84`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/194#discussion_r3214431464) and [`prepare-release.ts:90`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/194#discussion_r3214431582).
- No replies were added and no comments were minimized.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Existing-release updates drop false publish flags</summary>

**Cause:** [`publish-release.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/39e20592bdedda85750373a35a64d42318b19d8e/.agent/src/cli/publish-release.ts#L80-L85) only appends `--draft` and `--prerelease` when the parsed values are true. For `gh release edit`, publishing a draft requires an explicit `--draft=false`, and clearing prerelease similarly needs an explicit false value.

**Candidate solutions:** On the edit path, emit explicit `--draft=<bool>` and `--prerelease=<bool>` values, or fail unsupported false-state edits clearly. Add a focused regression test for updating an existing draft release with `draft=false`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Issue creation URL parse failures become misleading dispatch failures</summary>

**Cause:** [`prepare-release.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/39e20592bdedda85750373a35a64d42318b19d8e/.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts#L88-L93) falls back to issue number `0` when the created issue URL cannot be parsed, then emits an empty `issue_number`.

**Candidate solutions:** Fail immediately when the created issue URL cannot be parsed, logging the unexpected URL format. Add create-path coverage where `gh issue list` returns no reusable issue and `gh issue create` returns both valid and invalid URL shapes.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the remaining findings require concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

- [ ] Fail clearly when release prepare cannot parse the created issue number, and add focused create-path coverage.

@sepo-agent /answer 

Question: it seems the release publish route doesn't do much? (I thought we'd have agent support to produce a release message etc but it seems not)...

Also can we actually add a changelog file to track all the function changes?  

In that case we might have agent support for drafting the release plus editing the changelog?

You're reading it correctly: `Agent / Release / Publish` is intentionally thin right now. It is a maintainer-controlled publish step, not an agent drafting step. It checks repo/version/tag state and then creates or updates the GitHub Release; the generated notes file is currently just `Sepo vX.Y.Z`, so it does **not** produce meaningful release notes yet. See [`agent-release-publish.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.github/workflows/agent-release-publish.yml#L1-L73) and [`publish-release.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.agent/src/cli/publish-release.ts#L77-L98).

The agent-assisted part is currently `Agent / Release / Prepare`: it creates/reuses a release-prep issue, dispatches the normal implement workflow, and uses the release prompt to update release-related files and open a PR. That prompt already says to update "release notes, docs, or checklist entries," but there is no actual changelog file in the repo for it to edit yet. See [`agent-release-prepare.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.github/workflows/agent-release-prepare.yml#L42-L62), [`prepare-release.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts#L28-L48), and [`agent-release.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.github/prompts/agent-release.md#L6-L15).

Yes, I think adding a changelog is the right next increment. I would keep it small:

1. Add root `CHANGELOG.md` with an `Unreleased` section and version sections.
2. Update `.github/prompts/agent-release.md` so release prepare must draft the release message and edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Update `.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts` acceptance criteria so the tracking issue explicitly requires changelog updates.
4. Optionally update publish so the GitHub Release notes come from the matching `CHANGELOG.md` version section instead of the current placeholder.
5. Add focused tests around the publish note extraction only if we wire publish to changelog content.

That keeps the split clean: **prepare is agentic** and drafts/edits changelog content in a PR; **publish is manual** and only publishes the already-reviewed release notes after merge.

If approved, the follow-up implementation should be scoped to changelog + release prompt/publish note plumbing, without reintroducing a public `/release` route.

@sepo-agent /answer

2. Further I think we should add changelog in conjunction with the release? -> when we prosper releases of  the repo it will update the changelog accordingly (by listing recent PRs and fixes and add line by line feature changes)?  

Does it make sense? Or we should separate changelog into a separate pr?

Yes, that makes sense.

I’d recommend this split:

1. **In this PR #194:** remove publish entirely.
   - Drop `.github/workflows/agent-release-publish.yml`
   - Drop `.agent/src/cli/publish-release.ts`
   - Drop `.agent/src/__tests__/publish-release-cli.test.ts`
   - Trim publish-specific docs from [`versioning.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md#L38-L46)

   Keep only the useful prepare side: manual source-repo-gated release preparation that creates/reuses an issue and dispatches agent implementation with [`agent-release.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0ac43c1fc30c87592e9b44852502603bf5a4f9b4/.github/prompts/agent-release.md#L1-L35).

2. **In a follow-up PR:** add changelog + agent-assisted release drafting.
   - Add root `CHANGELOG.md`
   - Define a simple format, probably `Unreleased`, then `vX.Y.Z - YYYY-MM-DD`
   - Update the release prompt so the agent reviews recent merged PRs/fixes since the previous tag and writes curated line-by-line entries
   - Keep entries human-readable, not a raw dump of every commit
   - Categories could be `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`, `Internal`

3. **Later or same follow-up PR:** re-add publish only after it can consume the reviewed changelog/release notes.
   - Publish should not invent notes at publish time.
   - It should publish the already-reviewed changelog section for the version.

So: **yes to changelog as part of the release workflow**, but I’d separate it from this PR. This PR should become “release prepare only.” The next PR should be “release changelog + agent drafting,” and publish can come after that or inside that PR only if it stays small.
